claude_code.supported_min_source: the .claude-plugin/marketplace.json schema this catalog ships has been stable since 2.0.0; the previous floor was never validated
claude_code.verification_method: Live-CLI revalidation on 2026-10-07 — this run's runner has the `claude` CLI installed and `claude --version` reports `2.1.293 (Claude Code)`, matching the target exactly. `validated_against` and `latest_known` both advance from 2.1.286 to **2.1.293** together (no divergence), covering seven releases (2.1.287–2.1.293) in one pass. Reviewed every changelog entry across that range for catalog surface. Adopted/documented: **Claude Mods** (2.1.287), a new plugin component type that runs in-process on Claude Code and the Desktop Code tab — this catalog ships no `plugin.json` of its own (manifest-only, so it cannot carry a mod itself), but `tamirs-superpowers` already ships one (`mod/register.tsx`: an objective pane, a rate-limit band, a Desktop usage line, semantic skill suggestion, and definition-of-done/compaction hooks), confirmed by re-cloning that repo and running `claude plugin test .` live against it — 21/21 mod tests pass on 2.1.293. Documented in the install guide's What-you-get row and `docs/agent-guidelines/testing.md`. **`claude plugin validate` no longer skips a plugin folder that also holds a marketplace manifest** (2.1.289): directly relevant here, since all three listed plugin repos ship both `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` and `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` side by side for standalone installs (see 'Installing a plugin standalone instead') — re-ran `claude plugin validate --strict --json` against each on the live 2.1.289+ CLI and this time plugin.json is genuinely checked (headhunter: 3 pre-existing unknown-field warnings, unchanged from last pass; tamirs-superpowers and jose-claudinho: clean). Noted in `docs/agent-guidelines/testing.md` as the reason a prior audit on an older CLI could have silently skipped these. **`claude plugin validate`'s gating-hooks report** (2.1.290, `--json`'s `gatingHooks` array): ran it against this catalog's own manifest (empty — no plugin.json here) and, as a deeper audit, against `tamirs-superpowers`' `mod/register.tsx`, which surfaced 4 gating hooks (`agent.spawn`, `prompt.submit`, `tool.call`, `session.compact`) with no `.catch` — flagged in Future opportunities for that repo's own nightly, since it ships no source here. Also as part of this audit, the previously-flagged `tamirs-superpowers` hooks.json issue (27 unquoted-`${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` warnings, noted in the 2.1.286 pass) is now **confirmed fixed upstream** — `claude plugin validate --strict` on its current `plugin.json` reports zero warnings for `hooks/hooks.json`. **Plugin/skill name length cap** (2.1.292: names over 256 chars are now ignored): checked every name in this catalog's manifest and the three plugin repos' own manifests — the longest is `tamirs-superpowers` at 19 characters, nowhere near the cap, so nothing is silently dropped. **`claude plugin test` reports mod test failures instead of passing silently** (2.1.292, re: `expect` inside a hook): re-ran it live against `tamirs-superpowers`' mod suite (the only one of the three with a mod) — 21 pass, 0 fail. **`claude plugin install --marketplace <source>` now adds the marketplace first if it isn't already added** (2.1.292, previously it only selected among already-added marketplaces): documented in the install guide's Useful-flags section as a genuine one-step alternative to the two-command `marketplace add` + `install` flow for any of this catalog's three plugins. Reviewed and found no further catalog surface: 2.1.287's MCP server URL prompts/elicitation and `n:<text>` agents-view filter (no manifest-facing surface; this catalog ships no `.mcp.json`), the `alwaysLoad:false` semantics change (no surface, no `.mcp.json` here); 2.1.288's `$.ui.selection()` mod API, built-in `gh api` for cloud sessions, `--max-findings` for `/code-review` (mod/host-UI, no manifest surface); 2.1.289's `agent.spawn` for teammates and idle/waiting agent states (mod API only), the Bash deny/ask bypass fix (host security, no manifest surface); 2.1.290's `serverToolUses`/`tool.check` `agentId`+`ceiling` mod-hook additions and `ThemeKey`/`Color` mod-hook typings (mod-dev surface only — relevant to `tamirs-superpowers`' own `.tsx` mod, not to this manifest-only catalog), the WebFetch `offset` and dialog-timeout fixes (host-side); 2.1.291 (bug fixes only, no catalog-facing entries); 2.1.292's `prompt.autocomplete` mod event, `$.model.complete` prompt caching, and workflow agents in `agent.spawn` (mod API only), the stdio MCP protocol-negotiation default change (no `.mcp.json` here); and 2.1.293's Claude Haiku 5.5 and `subagentStatusLine` `agentType` (no manifest surface), `isDeferred` on `$.tool.register` for mods (relevant to a mod registering its own tools — `tamirs-superpowers`' mod registers none today, so no action), and the HTTP MCP memory-leak fix (no `.mcp.json` in this catalog). Platform-specific and host/session/UI-only entries across 2.1.287–2.1.293 not named above have zero marketplace-manifest, plugin-source, or skill-loading surface. `make validate` (regenerate + validate manifests, `make agent:check`, 3 plugins in sync, no drift), `make validate-skills` (`claude plugin validate --strict --json .agents/skills`), `make assert-contract`, `scripts/check-platform-targets.sh --assert-current`, and `claude plugin validate --strict .` on the marketplace manifest all pass clean against the live 2.1.293 CLI. `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`, `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json`, and `.cursor-plugin/marketplace.json` needed no schema change across the whole 2.1.287–2.1.293 range. Only Claude Code entries in this shared platform-target file were touched; Cursor, Codex, and OpenCode values are untouched. Prior verification (2026-09-30): 2.1.286 was confirmed live and reviewed for the 2.1.282 → 2.1.286 delta — see the install guide's per-version sections for full history.

cursor.supported_min_source: Cursor documents no minimum version for plugins; the floor is the version actually validated rather than guessed. The previous 0.45.0 floor predates Cursor's plugin system entirely
cursor.verification_method: latest desktop build from official Cursor download links (3.18.9, 2026-08-30 stable) cross-checked against cursor.com/changelog (feature 3.11; date-only entries through 2026-09-02 Self-Hosted Machines / Team Pools / partner sandboxes / computer use); team-marketplace import is a Dashboard flow

codex.supported_min_source: earliest release this catalog has claimed .agents/plugins/marketplace.json support for
codex.verification_method: documentary revalidation by this repo's standing Codex method (official release notes plus catalog compatibility review; the Codex CLI is not installed on the review machine). Reviewed every openai/codex release from 0.148.0 through 0.153.4 for plugin/marketplace changes: #41208 (0.151.0) reports invalid project marketplaces without hiding valid plugins, #41953 (0.153.0) enforces a marketplace source policy for OpenAI-curated plugins only, and #42149/#42150 (0.153.0) upgrade Git marketplaces from merged configuration and add remote-marketplace support to the plugin CLI. None alter the portable Agent Plugin catalog shape, so .agents/plugins/marketplace.json remains discoverable unchanged; 0.153.0 widens how it can be consumed rather than narrowing it.

opencode.supported_min_source: oldest version on which `skills.paths` discovery of a catalog plugin's skills was verified with `opencode debug skill`
opencode.verification_method: `opencode --version` on the maintainer machine (reported 1.18.29); latest from registry.npmjs.org/opencode-ai. OpenCode has no marketplace, so the catalog itself cannot be installed — skill discovery is verified directly with `opencode debug skill`, pointing `skills.paths` at this repo's `.agents/skills` and confirming `run-plugins-catalog` resolves to its `SKILL.md`

capability_gaps.marketplace: OpenCode has no plugin marketplace and no plugin manifest, so this catalog cannot be added as an install source. Each plugin repo is installed directly — clone it and point `skills.paths` at its `skills/` directory, or symlink it into the OpenCode skills directory. Every plugin in this catalog ships its own `opencode.json` and its own OpenCode install guide.
capability_gaps.catalog_discovery: There is no OpenCode equivalent of listing plugins from a remote catalog. The plugin table in this repo's README is the discovery surface; installation is then per-repo.
